synthetic

sin-THET-ik — stress the THET; think 'synthesizer': machine-made sound, machine-made stuff. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Synthetic is made artificially by people rather than occurring in nature; not genuine.

The jacket was made from synthetic fibers designed to imitate wool.

Worked Example

In the lab, chemists combine petroleum compounds under heat and pressure. The result is a stretchy material that looks and feels exactly like rubber. But it never dripped from any tree.

A material built by people to imitate a natural one is synthetic. Unlike 'fake,' which implies worthlessness or deception, synthetic items genuinely work — they just aren't natural in origin.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

artificial: Artificial is the broad word for anything made by people instead of nature — artificial light, artificial flavoring, an artificial deadline. Synthetic is more specific: chemically manufactured, usually in a lab or factory, often to stand in for a natural material. Everything synthetic is artificial, but an artificial pond has nothing synthetic in it.

manmade: Manmade says only that people produced it rather than nature — a manmade lake is still ordinary water. Synthetic tells you how: assembled from chemical ingredients that never occurred in nature. A manmade canal can be dug through natural rock and contain nothing synthetic at all.

imitation: Imitation describes purpose — the thing is made to copy the look of something real, like imitation leather on a car seat. Synthetic describes origin: built by people from chemicals rather than found in nature. A synthetic fiber may imitate wool, or it may copy nothing at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

natural: produced by nature

genuine: real and authentic

Where it sits · how far from natural it is — processed → synthetic → counterfeit

processed vs. synthetic: Processed is weaker than synthetic — processed cheese starts as real cheese that humans altered, while a synthetic material is built entirely from scratch.

counterfeit vs. synthetic: Counterfeit is stronger than synthetic: a synthetic diamond is openly lab-made, but a counterfeit one is manufactured specifically to deceive.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — syn-

prefix — syn-: together (Greek)

root — thet-

root — thet-: to put, to place (Greek)

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: relating to (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek syn- (together) plus thet- (to put) means 'put together.' Something synthetic has been assembled by people from parts rather than grown by nature.

Use the root in a new word: photosynthesis

Use the root in a new word: photosynthesis: Through photosynthesis, plants put together sunlight, water, and air to make their own food.

Word Choice

Synthetic is literal for lab-made materials like fibers and rubber, and slightly negative when applied to feelings — a 'synthetic smile' is an insincere one.
